newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian econ minister sees harvest at 75-77 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russian econ minister sees harvest at 75-77 mln T.

text.p: Russia's economy ministry on Tuesday stuck to a government forecast that the 1996 net grain harvest would be 75-77 million tonnes.
Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin told a news conference that such output would almost entirely meet domestic demand.
Last year's drought-hit harvest was officially put at 63.4 million tonnes.

Interfax news agency quoted Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha, in charge of the harvest, as telling a ministry conference that Russia would have sufficent grain volumes to fill its strategic food reserves, which are used to feed the army and northern cities.
The reserves would total four million tonnes, he was quoted as saying.
But the ministry's Ivan Gridasov, who overseas crop-growing, told the conference that only 320,000 tonnes had been purchased so far.
Interfax quoted Gridasov as expressing "serious concern" over the slow pace of the harvest in the Siberian and Urals regions of Omsk, Tomsk, Chelyabinsk and Sverdlovsk.
Gridasov said that as of Monday, Russia had threshed 54 million tonnes of grain, or six million tonnes more than at the same time last year.
About 16 million hectares remained to be harvested, including 13 million in Siberia and the Urals regions, out of a total sown area of 53.8 million.
